Cross-Platform Builds > Releases and npm Publishing

Releases and npm Publishing

This chapter takes you from “builds successfully locally” to “users can install it directly”: first produce binaries for 6 platforms, then publish a GitHub Release, and finally publish the npm packages in dependency order. The example versions are sa 0.1.8 / sla 0.1.8; replace <VER> and <SLAVER> in the commands with the version being released (the bare version number, without a v). The two repositories are released on the same version line but are still independent npm packages: sla depends on the same-generation sa with an exact pin, and version numbers must not drift via ^.

Version Number Consistency

Before releasing, align every version number that will be written into a product; missing one place leads to “the package is new but the binary is still the old version”, or npm dependencies resolving to an old platform package.

RepositoryPlaces that must be kept in sync
sciThe .version in build.zig.zon; npm/packages/*/package.json (7: 6 platform packages + the meta package); the git tag; the Release asset names
sa_plugin_slaThe default sla_version in build.zig; npm/packages/*/package.json (7); the meta package's optionalDependencies; the meta package's exact dependency on @salang/sa; the default version in fetch-*-binaries; npm/README.md; the git tag; the Release asset names
# 构建机预检：6 个平台二进制是否都已 stage（缺文件则非零退出）
cd sci && sh npm/tools/check-versions.sh
cd sa_plugin_sla && sh npm/tools/check-sla-versions.sh

# 依赖关系必须精确 pin，不能出现 ^ 或跨版本
node -p "require('./sci/npm/packages/sa/package.json').version"
node -p "require('./sa_plugin_sla/npm/packages/sla/package.json').dependencies['@salang/sa']"

The sla meta package depends on the same generation of the @salang/sa compiler (for example 0.1.8), because sla build-wasm needs sa to have LLVM-C; therefore the publishing order is always sa first, sla second.

1. Build the Products for 6 Platforms

The native Linux x86_64 build enables LLVM-C by default (needs llvm-14-dev), and its products fully support build-wasm; cross targets use -Dllvm=false and take the bootstrap route — smaller, but wasm can only use the C fallback. Pass -Dversion explicitly, so that whenever the tag is made it does not affect the version embedded in the binary.

cd sci

# Linux x86_64（LLVM 启用；放最后构建，避免 artifacts 被交叉构建覆盖）
zig build -Dversion=<VER> -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe \
  -p /tmp/sa-dist/linux-x86_64

# 交叉目标（bootstrap）
zig build -Dtarget=aarch64-linux-gnu -Dllvm=false -Dversion=<VER> \
  -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe -p /tmp/sa-dist/arm-aarch64
zig build -Dtarget=aarch64-macos -Dllvm=false -Dversion=<VER> \
  -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe -p /tmp/sa-dist/mac-aarch64
zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-macos -Dllvm=false -Dversion=<VER> \
  -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe -p /tmp/sa-dist/mac-x86_64
zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-windows-gnu -Dllvm=false -Dversion=<VER> \
  -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe -p /tmp/sa-dist/windows-x86_64

# FreeBSD（需要 sysroot，见 FreeBSD 章节）
SA_VERSION=<VER> sh tools/build_freebsd.sh --prefix /tmp/sa-dist/freebsd-x86_64

Every sla platform build must point at the same platform's sa standard library directory; a cross build that omits -Dsa-std-dir will link against the host machine's library.

cd sa_plugin_sla
for t in linux-x86_64 arm-aarch64 mac-aarch64 mac-x86_64 windows-x86_64 freebsd-x86_64; do
  zig build -Dversion=<SLAVER> -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe \
    -Dsa-std-dir=/tmp/sa-dist/$t/lib -p /tmp/sla-dist/$t
done

# 冒烟：只有 Linux / 当前主机产物能直接执行
/tmp/sla-dist/linux-x86_64/bin/sla --version        # sla <SLAVER>
/tmp/sa-dist/linux-x86_64/bin/sa --version          # sa <VER>
file /tmp/sla-dist/windows-x86_64/bin/sla.exe       # PE32+
file /tmp/sla-dist/mac-aarch64/bin/sla              # Mach-O arm64

2. Package the Release Assets

Asset names are a hard contract of fetch-*-binaries and cannot be renamed: sa-<VER>-<target>.zip and sla-<SLAVER>-<target>.zip. The sa zip contains at least sa/sa.exe, and should ideally include hubproxy as well; the sla zip contains bin/ and lib/ (the plugin library and sap.json), and the fetch script picks sla/sla.exe out of whatever path they are in.

cd /tmp/sa-dist
for d in linux-x86_64 arm-aarch64 mac-aarch64 mac-x86_64 \
         windows-x86_64 freebsd-x86_64; do
  (cd "$d/bin" && zip -q "/tmp/sa-<VER>-$d.zip" sa* hubproxy*)
done

cd /tmp/sla-dist
for d in linux-x86_64 arm-aarch64 mac-aarch64 mac-x86_64 \
         windows-x86_64 freebsd-x86_64; do
  (cd "$d" && zip -qr "/tmp/sla-<SLAVER>-$d.zip" bin lib)
done

unzip -l /tmp/sa-<VER>-windows-x86_64.zip   | grep -E 'sa\.exe|hubproxy'
unzip -l /tmp/sla-<SLAVER>-windows-x86_64.zip | grep -E 'sla\.exe|sla\.dll'

3. Commit, Tag, and Publish the GitHub Release

cd sci
git add build.zig.zon npm/packages <本次源码文件>
git commit -m "release: sa <VER>"
git tag -a <VER> -m "SA <VER>"
git push origin main <VER>          # 需要可写 token

GH_TOKEN="$GIT_TOKEN" gh release create <VER> /tmp/sa-<VER>-*.zip \
  --repo layola13/sci --title "SA <VER>" --notes "..."

cd sa_plugin_sla
git add build.zig npm sap.json src
git commit -m "release: sla <SLAVER>"
git tag -a <SLAVER> -m "SLA <SLAVER>"
git push origin master <SLAVER>

GH_TOKEN="$GIT_TOKEN" gh release create <SLAVER> /tmp/sla-<SLAVER>-*.zip \
  --repo layola13/sa_plugin_sla --title "SLA <SLAVER>" --notes "..."

After pushing the tag, check that the assets are 6 zips, and spot-check that one URL returns 200; the fetch script constructs this URL directly, and a missing asset will 404 on the publishing machine.

4. npm Publishing (the Windows 11 Real-Machine Flow)

The Windows publishing machine does not need to recompile; it only pulls the already-built binaries from the Release. The script requirement is PowerShell 5.1 (bundled with Win11) or 7, either works; the current scripts have dropped the 7.0 hard requirement and explicitly enable TLS 1.2.

4.1 Login and Preflight Checks

cd E:\projects\sla\sci
git pull
npm login
npm whoami        # 必须是有 @salang / @slalang 发布权限的账号

4.2 Publish @salang/sa First (Package by Package)

cd E:\projects\sla\sci\npm
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\fetch-binaries.ps1
# 默认 <VER>；版本不同则加 -Version <VER>
# 输出 [ok] all platform binaries staged under npm/packages/*/bin

cd packages
cd sa-linux-x64;     npm publish --access public
cd ..\sa-linux-arm64; npm publish --access public
cd ..\sa-darwin-arm64; npm publish --access public
cd ..\sa-darwin-x64;  npm publish --access public
cd ..\sa-win32-x64;   npm publish --access public
cd ..\sa-freebsd-x64; npm publish --access public
cd ..\sa;             npm publish --access public

Publish only one package at a time, so that on a real failure you can stop immediately at the last success point. The order is fixed: the 6 @salang/sa-<platform> packages first, and the @salang/sa meta package last; every scoped package must carry --access public.

4.3 Then Publish @slalang/sla (Package by Package)

cd E:\projects\sla\sa_plugin_sla
git pull
cd npm
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\fetch-sla-binaries.ps1
# 默认 <SLAVER>；同时把 sla_std/ 拷进 meta 包

cd packages
cd sla-linux-x64;     npm publish --access public
cd ..\sla-linux-arm64; npm publish --access public
cd ..\sla-darwin-arm64; npm publish --access public
cd ..\sla-darwin-x64;  npm publish --access public
cd ..\sla-win32-x64;   npm publish --access public
cd ..\sla-freebsd-x64; npm publish --access public
cd ..\sla;             npm publish --access public

Do not publish everything at once with a loop/batch script: once a platform package already has the same version, npm returns 403 and aborts, and the state of the later packages becomes hard to judge. When publishing package by package, after a failure continue from the next unpublished package.

4.4 Alternative Forms and 2FA

# 已安装 PowerShell 7：脚本命令把 powershell 换成 pwsh
pwsh -File tools\fetch-binaries.ps1

# 账号强制 2FA：给每条 npm publish 追加 OTP
npm publish --access public --otp=123456

5. Post-Publish Verification

npm view @salang/sa version
npm view @salang/sa-linux-x64 version
npm view @slalang/sla version
npm view @slalang/sla-linux-x64 version

# 干净目录安装，验证 launcher + 平台包 + sa 依赖链
mkdir %TEMP%\sla-npm-test
cd /d %TEMP%\sla-npm-test
npm init -y
npm i @slalang/sla
npx sa --version
npx sla --version
npx sla help

Then run a minimal build once more (on Windows build-wasm takes the C fallback, while build-c and build-js work normally):

npx sla build-c demo.sla -o demo.c
npx sla build-js demo.sla -o demo.js
npx sla build-wasm demo.sla -o demo.wasm   # 仅 C 回退覆盖的语法

6. Common Traps

PhenomenonCause / handling
script cannot be run because it contained a "#requires" statement for Windows PowerShell 7.0 You used an old script or an old checkout: git pull and rerun; the new script is #Requires -Version 5.1, or switch to pwsh
The argument 'npm\tools\...' to the -File parameter does not exist The current directory is already inside npm, so the path must not include npm\ again; from the npm directory use tools\fetch-binaries.ps1
The Invoke-WebRequest connection is closed PS 5.1 has not enabled TLS 1.2; the script already sets it — if it still fails, upgrade to PowerShell 7
403 Forbidden / E404 (scoped packages) The account is not in the @salang/@slalang organization, or the first publish omitted --access public (the script already includes it)
npm ERR! 403 ... You cannot publish over the previously published versions npm versions cannot be overwritten. If <VER> was already published, bump the patch version and redo the whole flow; do not change only the tag, and do not change the version of only the already-published platform packages — all 7 sla packages must share one version
After installation, @slalang/sla reports a missing platform package The platform packages were not published first, or the meta package's optionalDependencies do not match this release's version; publish the 6 platform packages first, then the meta package
libLLVM-14.so.1: cannot open shared object file (Linux) The 0.1.8 Linux assets dynamically link LLVM 14: the user installs llvm-14/libllvm14t64, or libLLVM-14.so.1 is placed into the platform package's bin/ as well; check-versions.sh warns about this
On macOS/Windows, build-wasm reports LLVM-C unavailable These two platforms' official assets are -Dllvm=false bootstraps; if you need full wasm, install LLVM 14 locally and build natively, or use the subset supported by the C fallback
After extraction on Windows, bin/sla has no execute bit The launcher automatically does chmod 0755 before spawnSync; do not bypass the sla command and execute the binary directly
artifacts/sa_std/libsa_std.a appears in the diff A build side effect; when only verifying, restore it with git checkout -- artifacts/sa_std/libsa_std.a; if it is to be released with the version, commit it explicitly and say so

7. End-to-End Checklist

  1. Align the version numbers → preflight with check-versions.sh / check-sla-versions.sh.
  2. Build sa for 6 platforms (Linux last, LLVM enabled) → build sla for 6 platforms.
  3. Make 6+6 zips and spot-check the Windows/Linux entries.
  4. Commit, tag, and push; create the two GitHub Releases and confirm the 12 assets.
  5. Win11: git pull → npm login → fetch sa → publish sa package by package.
  6. Win11: fetch sla → publish sla package by package (always after sa).
  7. npm view + a clean-directory install + npx sla help + a minimal-build regression.
  8. Documentation sync: keep this chapter's versions/commands consistent with sci/docs/release_process_cn.md.
